cands.bio: Republican member of the Alabama House of Representatives for District 91 since November 2018. Owned and ran Goodson Tire & Auto in Enterprise for more than 26 years, then sold it in 2023. Won the August 2026 Republican primary for U.S. House District 2.

endorsements.text: Endorsed by President Donald Trump for U.S. House District 2.

cands.gaps: We found no documented positions from Marques on data centers, large development or growth limits. We found nothing showing what he did, as opposed to said, on homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, or school choice and teacher pay. We found no specific bill or action of his on police pay, public-order penalties, or immigration enforcement beyond campaign statements. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. The 2019 fuel-tax vote reported by Wikipedia comes from a short, unsourced summary, so it is not used here. No notable controversies turned up in the pages reviewed.

cands.bio: Democrat and attorney from Mobile, serving as U.S. Representative for Alabama's 2nd District since January 2025. Previously a federal law clerk, White House and Justice Department aide, counsel to Sen. Sherrod Brown, and deputy chief of staff to Attorney General Merrick Garland.

endorsements.text: Campaign site lists endorsements from former Attorney General Loretta Lynch, Birmingham Mayor Randall Woodfin, Montgomery Mayor Steven Reed, Rep. Terri Sewell, former Gov. Don Siegelman and State Sen. Vivian Davis Figures.
Campaign site lists organizational endorsements from Planned Parenthood Action Fund, Giffords PAC, the Teamsters (IBT) and the League of Conservation Voters.
Former President Barack Obama endorsed him in the 2024 race.

cands.gaps: We found no statements or actions by Figures on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, slowing development, or school vouchers and charters. We found no documented stance on gun-rights measures such as red-flag laws or suppressors beyond his general pledge to address gun violence. We found no documented controversies and no foreign ties. His birth and upbringing in Mobile are documented, but the pages we read give no detail on his residence history beyond his schooling and career. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey, so his stated positions come mainly from his own campaign sites.

votes.what: Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.

votes.bill: S. 1071 / FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (final)
votes.what: Final FY2026 defense policy and funding-authorization bill (about $900 billion), carried in the House on the vehicle S. 1071.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Nov. 12 final, ended the shutdown)
votes.what: Ended the 43-day federal shutdown: funds government through Jan. 30, 2026 and three full-year spending bills.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Sept. 19 House passage)
votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.bill: H.R. 881 (2025) DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act
votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.
Requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

votes.bill: H.R. 1968 (2025) Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).

votes.bill: H.R. 152 (2025) Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.
